headline: Cleverbridge has still not said how many people were affected, which companies' customers, or how the intruders got in.
summary: Check, nothing new. Re-read Cleverbridge's incident page (s001): wording unchanged since the Nov 23 revision, with notification begun Nov 20, CVV data in a minority of cases, not ransomware. No count (q002), no list of affected companies beyond what the story has (q004), no cause or attacker (q005). Cleverbridge's status page shows all systems operational. Its own client stories still name the sellers already listed; being a client does not show a company's buyers were affected. Hacker News: three link posts, none with comments.
author: Research agent

headline: The page now says what Cleverbridge is; no finding changed.

headline: Cleverbridge has still not said how many people were affected, how the intruders got in, or who they are.
summary: Company incident page (s001) re-read, unchanged since the Nov 23 revision. Open questions re-checked: no count, no named affected brands beyond Malwarebytes, no state attorney general filing found, no German data-protection authority statement, no root cause, no attacker claim in press. New coverage only relays the company page and BleepingComputer (heise online, ThaiCERT, Hungary's National Cybersecurity Institute); no new fact. No claim or label changed. Privacy check done.

headline: Cleverbridge now says the CVV security code was taken in a minority of cases, and calls the theft a limited amount of personal data.
summary: Company incident page (Tier 1, s001) re-read and found revised since the Nov 22 archived copy: it now says a third party copied 'a limited amount of personal data ... including a small amount of payment card data' (was: 'payment card data'), and that 'in a minority of cases' the information included CVV data. Added c014 (Confirmed, company page). Updated c001 wording and detail, c004, c009 and c012 details, q001 and q002 answers, known, not_known and size_basis. Added the archived Nov 22 copy as s001's archive link. Also folds in the u003 changes (The Register, s006), which were not yet merged. c004 stays Reported: the full field lists come from notices quoted by outlets. Checked: no state attorney general filing (Washington list), no German or other regulator statement, no new affected-brand notice, no attacker claim in press, no new count. Staleness check done. Privacy check done: no reporters, staff, handles or contacts named. No label changes on existing claims.
